description:
checkout.commitPlace the order: obtain the user's payment approval when needed, give you an approved virtual credit card to enter, and submit at the order control you name.

Supply the checkout reference and the control that places the order: its reference in `submit_ref`, or a description in `submit_look` when it has none. The call pays for the terms your latest `checkout.inspect` recorded, so inspect the checkout again when its terms change. When no approval covers the terms, it shows the user the payment approval with those terms and a capture of the page, and waits for their decision. Once the user approves, the same call goes on: it gives you a virtual credit card to enter, applies the approved payment, or presses the order control on the view you named it on. When the page changed meanwhile, the press is refused; observe the page and call again. The runtime reuses an approval that still covers the checkout, as described in your checkout instructions. For `payment_route: wallet`, the runtime opens wallet payment approval automatically. A `merchant_saved` route pays with the selected method already stored by this merchant. A `takeover` route leaves completion to the user and does not submit. Continue through the available checkout steps, then report `needs_input` with `reason: payment` and the remaining steps for the user. When a virtual credit card is returned, use its number, expiry, CVC and any provided billing address to fill out the checkout form with `browser.act`, just as you would with any credit card. Enter only a credit card returned by the runtime. On a credit card entry page before the final order control, call with `submit_ref` and `submit_look` null to obtain it.

username_field.description: The reference of the visible, editable username, email or phone field for the current sign-in step, from controls; null when absent, read-only or disabled, including a read-only account identifier on a password-only step.

password_field.description: The reference of the visible, editable password field for the current sign-in step, from controls; null when absent, read-only or disabled.

google_button.description: The reference of the visible Google sign-in control, whatever element it is, such as a button, a link or a framed button; null when the page shows none.

apple_button.description: The reference of the visible Apple sign-in control, whatever element it is, such as a button, a link or a framed button; null when the page shows none.

amazon_button.description: The reference of the visible Amazon sign-in control, whatever element it is, such as a button, a link or a framed button; null when the page shows none.

previous_attempt.description: What the page shows about an earlier sign-in attempt: rejected when it shows one failed, such as a wrong password message, none when it shows no earlier attempt, unknown otherwise.
